title: Pressure in Fluids

problems_fixed.what: Duplicate solution within bronze tier: B1 and B3 both solved to 5000. Changed B3 pressure 50,000 Pa to 60,000 Pa so force becomes 6000 N (distinct). Updated display, solutions, misconception expect (600,000) and guided_steps.

old.display: A pressure of 50,000 Pa acts over an area of 0.1 m². Calculate the force.

new.display: A pressure of 60,000 Pa acts over an area of 0.1 m². Calculate the force.

opener_concept: Same 60 N of weight under a snowshoe (2 m2) versus a stiletto heel (0.01 m2): the student divides force by area twice (30 vs 6000) and discovers pressure = F/A by common sense before the equation is named. Extends to p = h rho g for liquids.
